newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Support for Austria's conservatives falls - poll.
newsitem.headline: Support for Austria's conservatives falls - poll.

text.p: Austria's conservative People's Party lost another two percent in an opinion poll published on Wednesday after alleged insults of foreign politicians and officials by its leader Wolfgang Schuessel.
The poll, published in Der Standard newspaper, showed backing for the junior coalition partner of the dominant Social Democrats falling to 22 percent.
Chancellor Viktor Klima's Social Democrats scored 36 percent while the far-right Freedom Party of populist Joerg Haider came in second place with a rating of 28 percent, the poll showed.
The leftist Greens and Liberal Forum scored eight and six percent respectively.
Of those questioned, 45 percent did not believe Schuessel's denial that he had ever called Bundesbank President Hans Tietmeyer "a real pig".
Only 34 percent believed Schuessel, the foreign minister who endured an 80-minute grilling on the subject in parliament on Tuesday.
Just 10 percent said they would vote for Schuessel as chancellor, behind Haider at 18 percent and Klima at 36 percent.
